name: Reading list
status: Started 27 Nov 2026 with the baseball books of Robert Whiting. The 'Read?' column is for the owner: tell Claude when you finish a book and what you thought, and it will be recorded here.
summary: Books that explain the stories on this site: how Japanese players, clubs and agents think, and why moving to America was so hard for so long. Each row says what the book is about, why it matters for a page on this site, and what to search for, because some books changed their title.
quick_facts: You Gotta Have Wa (1989, updated 2009): the owner's first pick
'The Meaning of Ichiro' (2004 hardcover) is sold today as 'The Samurai Way of Baseball' (2005 paperback, revised). Same book, new name
💲 Books cost money. Free options: your public library, or its e-book app. Whiting also writes online at Substack, where some posts are free

sections.title: In short
sections.intro: Robert Whiting is an American who has lived in Tokyo for most of the last sixty years and is widely called the leading English-language writer on Japanese baseball. His books are the background to three pages on this site: Hideo Nomo, Don Nomura, and (through a reported friendship) Shawn Novak.

sections.title: Robert Whiting: baseball books
sections.intro: In order of publication. 'On this site' says which page the book helps with.

cells: The Chrysanthemum and the Bat
菊とバット
His first book: how Japan plays the same game differently. He says he wrote it on a bet. Time magazine named it the best sports book of its year.
Background for everything

You Gotta Have Wa
1989 (updated edition 2009)
和をもって日本となす (Kadokawa, translated by Masayuki Tamaki; paperback in two volumes)

American players in Japan, and the idea of 'wa' (和, group harmony): the team before the individual. Named one of the top 50 baseball books of the last half-century by the baseball research society SABR.

rows: Born in New Jersey in 1942, raised in Eureka, California. Came to Tokyo with the US Air Force in 1962 and studied at Sophia University.
https://sabr.org/journal/article/henry-chadwick-award-robert-whiting/
Best known for You Gotta Have Wa, which Wikipedia says sold 125,000 copies; the writer David Halberstam said it applies to almost every side of US–Japan relations.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Whiting
Winner of SABR's Henry Chadwick Award for baseball research.
https://sabr.org/awards/winner/robert-whiting/
Still active: he gave a lecture on baseball and US–Japan diplomacy at Occidental College in Los Angeles on 9 Sept 2025.
https://www.oxy.edu/academics/global-engagement/young-initiative/events/diamond-diplomacy-robert-whiting-traces-history
Link to this site (RUMOUR, not fact): Weekly Jitsuwa quoted an unnamed insider in Feb 2026 saying agent Shawn Novak is close to him.
https://weekly-jitsuwa.jp/archives/22720

rows: A caution this site already applies: on the Nomo page some details rest on Whiting alone. He is the standard source, but one author is still one author. My observation.
https://anishimori123.github.io/News/sports/baseball/hideo-nomo.html

His books side with the players against the clubs, and the 1999 book is built on Don Nomura's own account. Read them as one side of the argument, the side this site's club sources do not give. My observation.
